Ipswich Town v Aston Villa (Kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from Portman Road. When these teams faced each other here in a top-flight clash two season ago they shared the spoils in a 2-2 draw that saw the goals scored by players who have since moved on to other clubs, with Liam Delap getting both for the Tractor Boys, while Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins struck for the Villains.

Brighton \u0026 Hove Albion v Newcastle United (Kick-off 2.05pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from AMEX Stadium. Danny Welbeck scored twice in a 2-1 win here for the Seagulls last season, while Nick Woltemade, currently on loan at Juventus, replied with one of his eight goals for the Magpies, which at the time leveled the contest eight minutes before Welbeck found the winner.

Arsenal v Manchester City (Kick-off 4.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from Emirates Stadium. The Gunners laid down a marker for this season with a statement 3-0 win over the Citizens in the Community Shield back in August, and took the lead after just 23 seconds of that contest through Riccardo Calafiori. Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard also got their names on the scoresheet in a totally dominant display for the Premier League champions, as City slipped to defeat in the first match of the post-Pep Guardiola era.

Coventry City v Ipswich Town (Kick-off 8.00pm). Coverage of the top-flight match from Coventry Building Society Arena. The Tractor Boys come into this clash having won the last five meetings against the Sky Blues, four of which were in the Championship and one in the FA Cup. In the games last season they triumphed 3-0 at Portman Road and then came here later the same month to claim a 2-0 victory, with Jack Clarke and Wes Burns getting the goals in the second-half.
